neighbours.label: The prefix piece ' mis' or ' over' split off at the start of a verb in a slot that calls for the verb's -ing form (after keep/kept/keeps, stop, is/are/was/were, constantly, always); the same prefix starting a base-form or past-tense verb (after to, will, might, don't, have) or a noun stays low, and other prefixes (re-, pre-, under-, out-) are weak.
neighbours.short: mis-/over- starting a verb in an -ing slot
fire: He keeps misreading the instructions on the label.
She kept overthinking every message before she sent it.
Please stop overreacting to small mistakes.
The kids were misbehaving all afternoon at the museum.
Our manager is constantly overestimating how fast we can work.
He always misplacing his keys is why we leave late.
They are overcharging tourists at the station kiosk.
My sister keeps mispronouncing the name of the town.
quiet: She can be reached at Linda@LeadinginContext.
He tends to misread the instructions on the label.
She overthought every message before she sent it.
Please don't overreact to small mistakes.
The kids might misbehave at the museum this afternoon.
Our manager will overestimate how fast we can work.
His misplacement of the keys is why we leave late.
They have overcharged tourists at the station kiosk.
neighbours.notes: Cold run (deep-cell experiment): labelled from own tops and probes only. Sentences written blind by a second author from the label alone; the globalMOO leak (repeated email '@') was placed as a near miss. Twin probes: the same prefix piece fired in -ing slots and stayed low in base/past slots. Risk: some over- verbs may tokenize without a separate ' over' piece.

predictions: 6/8 fire; the mis- items strongest, some over- items may not split off ' over'; near misses low
